phase3_findings.description: Fail-OPEN on an unreadable UNRECORDED tracked file: iter_blobs() skips an OSError file with only a stderr breadcrumb and never yields it, so a new/not-yet-baselined file (or a file that grew new pending occurrences) that is unreadable is absent from `pending`, the forward-direction AC3 new-occurrence guard never sees it, and cmd_check exits 0. The advertised 'fail-closed both ways' guarantee has a hole in its core direction. Realistically rare (an unreadable git-tracked path is unusual, esp. in CI), so advisory rather than blocking. Remedy: accumulate skipped paths and treat a non-empty skip set as RED.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: advisory — recommend failing closed on a non-empty skip set; not a merge blocker (test-only lint, near-impossible input in CI, no false green on any realistic input)

phase3_findings.description: 'audited {audited} of {audited} files' interpolates the same variable on both sides of 'of', so the X-of-Y idiom can never surface a shortfall — a run that skipped an unreadable file still prints N of N, reading as complete coverage. Behavior-inert observability nit (Phase 4.1.5 cap). Remedy: count total ls-files entries separately and emit a skipped tally.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: advisory — pairs with the fail-open fix; capped at Suggestion (behavior-inert)

phase3_findings.description: Interaction of best-effort unreadable-skip with fail-closed stale detection: an unreadable tracked file that HAS a baseline row is reported as a 'stale pending_sweep_baseline row — the file carries no pending occurrence any more' (RED), which mislabels the cause (transient unreadability, not a completed sweep). Fail-closed on exit code (no false green), but a misleading finding message.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: advisory — cosmetic mislabel of a rare failure; no false green

phase3_findings.description: The --print-population argparse help ('a provenance file emits both a pending and a frozen line') drops the module docstring's qualifier 'with both a value and a pending remainder'. A provenance file with only a value (no prose) emits only the frozen line, so the unqualified 'both' over-generalizes. True for every provenance file in the current data, so a clarity nit governed by the accurate docstring above it — not a documented falsehood.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: advisory — mirror the docstring qualifier in the help string

phase3_findings.description: main() checks args.update_baseline before args.print_population with no mutual-exclusion, so passing both silently rewrites the record and never prints the population. Minor UX; an argparse mutually-exclusive group or a documented precedence note would make it explicit.

Test gaps: (1) frozen-tooling bucket + the frozen bucket-name emission strings in --print-population are unasserted (only pending/frozen-provenance lines checked); (2) malformed/unreadable bucket JSON exit-2 contract untested; (3) count-BELOW-baseline partial-sweep drift untested (only count-above); (4) mid-scan unreadable-file skip untested; (5) repo_root cwd-fallback untested. The four RED fail-closed paths + --update-baseline idempotence (the load-bearing contract) ARE directly asserted.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: advisory — coverage of the load-bearing fail-closed contract is adequate; these are completeness improvements

phase3_findings.description: git ls-files -z subprocess in iter_blobs uses check=True with no handler in scan/cmd_check/main (unlike repo_root and the bucket-load path), so a git failure raises an uncaught CalledProcessError with a traceback instead of the module's own breadcrumb. Fail-closed on exit code (non-zero), so no silent-pass hazard — just inconsistent with the module's deliberate error surfacing.

The 3-line comment block below the #1745 run.sh section banner is mostly descriptive narrative rather than the specific wrong change prevented (only 'Drive the exit code and finding lines, not the prose' names a prevented mistake). Sits at the 3-line cap and reads as a conventional section header, so marginal under the prevention-only standard.

report:
Iteration-2 review of PR #1973 (issue #1745) at head 4f163d684. Scope: the fix delta over iteration 1's APPROVE WITH ADVISORY NOTES — module-docstring/help rewordings in lib/test/lint-brand-devflow-sweep.py and added run.sh coverage for --print-population (dual-line provenance emit) and --update-baseline (idempotent reseed leaves --check green).

Iteration-1 advisories RESOLVED (confirmed independently by code-reviewer, comment-analyzer, and the final-pass reviewer): the docstring now precisely states the count-UNbounded frozen-bucket rule (AC3 scopes the new-occurrence guard to occurrences OUTSIDE frozen buckets, so a new DevFlow inside a frozen bucket is allowed by design — verified against classify() returning pcount=0 for the three path-based frozen buckets and total-value only for provenance); the --print-population help/docstring correctly describes the one-or-more-lines-per-file contract and the provenance dual-emit; the unreadable-file skip is disclosed as a best-effort limit; and run.sh gains non-vacuous --print-population and --update-baseline assertions (specific output lines + idempotency, not vacuous green).

Phase 3.1.5 completeness-critic (forced by detect_all_audit): independently enumerated the brand-occurrence population by grep over git ls-files (a signal other than the lint's own classify) — 173 tracked files carry brand-cased DevFlow, and ALL 173 are covered by the bucket record (frozen prefixes/exact files/provenance or the pending baseline); 0 uncovered. The real-tree lint exits 0 (audited 1120 of 1120 files). The audit is a genuine superset of the independent signal — complete with respect to it.

Correctness: all agents confirm the enforcement mechanism satisfies the in-scope ACs (AC1 machine-checkable bucket classification; AC3 new-occurrence-outside-frozen turns RED; AC4/AC5/AC6 fail-closed reconciliation both directions, git ls-files -z worktree-immune population per #711, seeded baseline recorded). AC2's mass prose sweep is correctly out of scope (deferred). first-match ordering (record→historical→tooling→provenance→pending) is correct; provenance split total-value cannot go negative.

No Critical or blocking findings. The most substantive advisory is a fail-OPEN in iter_blobs: an unreadable UNRECORDED tracked file bypasses the forward-direction AC3 guard and exits 0 — a genuine hole in the 'fail-closed both ways' claim, but realistically rare (an unreadable git-tracked path, near-impossible in CI) and producing no false green on any realistic input; graded Important-advisory, recommend failing closed on a non-empty skip set (which also fixes the corroborated 'audited N of N' observability nit that can never surface a skip). Remaining items are Suggestion-level: the unreadable-file/stale-row mislabel, the --print-population help over-generalization, the update/print precedence, the ls-files check=True traceback, and five test-coverage gaps (frozen-tooling/bucket-name assertions, exit-2 malformed-JSON, count-below-baseline partial-sweep, mid-scan skip, repo_root fallback).

Verdict: APPROVE WITH ADVISORY NOTES — the fix delta is correct and the iteration-1 advisories are addressed; the new findings are all advisory and none blocks merge.
